text: Most colour advice is a static chart. You decide you are a winter, buy a foundation, and it is the wrong depth for your actual skin, because nothing ever looked at your face.
Chroma starts from the opposite end. It measures your face with the YouCam API, then computes everything else from those measurements.
This is the deployed app. You give it one photo. The analysis is a real call to the YouCam skin tone analysis endpoint. There is a recorded sample too, labelled as recorded, but I will run it live.
I choose the live path, pick a photo, and run the measurement. The photo goes to the YouCam skin tone analysis API, which returns the measured colours.

Four colours, straight from the API: skin, lips, eyes and brows, each with its measured lightness, chroma and hue. Nothing is averaged or filled in. The API did not return hair colour, so the app lists it as missing and lowers its confidence, rather than inventing a value.

From those four hex values, Chroma derives a seasonal profile. Here, Bright Spring. The app shows its work: every signal that voted on the undertone, and what each contributed. This is a styling framework, not a medical diagnosis.
The YouCam makeup engine accepts arbitrary hex colours, so the looks are not presets. Each is computed from the measured palette, and the exact transformation is printed under every swatch.
Now the try-on. I press render, and the computed look is sent to the YouCam makeup virtual try-on endpoint.
That is the composited image: the same photo, with the look computed from the measured colours. Nothing is a preset, and nothing is manually edited.

The same measurement drives the shopping advice. Any garment colour is scored against the palette with CIEDE2000, the perceptual distance the makeup engine uses, and the app suggests a colour that would work better.
Foundation is matched on depth first, undertone second, because the wrong depth is far more visible than slightly wrong warmth.
Measure, interpret, personalize, try on, compare. One measurement, and every recommendation traces back to it. That is the whole idea.
